messages:
jamal: Heads-up — canary traffic for the /generate endpoint stalled in eu-west-1. Canary pods are Pending because new gpu-pool nodes never provisioned. Looks like TF apply failed earlier and the workspace drifted. :rotating_light:

maria: :eyes: I saw a partial terraform run last night that errored midway. `terraform apply` hit a quota error on the cloud provider and left workspace in a partial state.

kevin: Logs from CI: 
```
Error: RateLimitExceeded: requests per minute exceeded for resource 'accelerator-pools'
  on modules/gpu_pool/main.tf line 42, in resource "cloud_gpu_pool" "redwood":
  42: resource "cloud_gpu_pool" "redwood" { ... }
```

kevin: provider returned 429s during autoscaler create which stopped the pool from reaching target size. Autoscaler then didn't register nodes so scheduler left canary pods Pending.

olivia: Canary rollout is at 30% and helm plugin keeps retrying traffic split. App metrics show increased error rate (502) for canary requests that did manage to land on undersized nodes. Suggest flip traffic back to stable and pause rollout.

sanjay: GitOps operator also shows reconcile errors: `kubectl -n redwood get events` -> `FailedCreatePodSandBox: failed to setup network for pod` — root cause seems to be CNI provisioning delays when new gpu nodes are initializing.

infra-bot: [ALERT] quota_exhausted for project-redwood-eu-west-1 at 2028-05-12T03:12:32Z. Affected resources: GPU quota, IP addresses. Ticket: INF-Q-9821.

jamal: Plan: 1) Abort canary traffic (roll back HelmTrafficSplit) 2) Mark TF workspace tainted for the failed module and run targeted apply with exponential backoff on provider rate limits 3) Coordinate with cloud to request temporary quota bump if needed 4) Postmortem after stable restored.

maria: For 2) I'll run `terraform state list` and `terraform apply -target=module.gpu_pool` with `TF_CLI_ARGS_apply="-parallelism=1"` to avoid concurrent API bursts.

kevin: I'll open a short-lived routing rule to divert canary traffic to stable: `kubectl patch trafficsplit redwood-gen -p '{"spec":{"backends":[{"service":"stable","weight":"100"}]}}'` — then monitor latency.

olivia: Doing the patch now. pinging @sanjay to watch for CNI flapping.

sanjay: Watching — CNI logs show a couple of ENI attachment timeouts. If the quota bump doesn't come quick, we should consider using existing spot pools as fallback.

jamal: Thanks team. I'll start the targeted TF apply after maria posts state output. Let's keep this thread for updates. I'll also create a follow-up: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3247

maria: `terraform state list` shows `module.gpu_pool.cloud_gpu_pool.redwood` present but with tainted instances. Preparing targeted apply.

kevin: Traffic flipped, canary -> stable. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: [INFO] INF-Q-9821 updated: temporary quota bump requested, awaiting approval.

jamal: Apply succeeded after lowering parallelism, nodes are joining, canary pods moving to Running. Will wait 5m healthy window before re-weighing.

olivia: Metrics look good so far. Re-weigh to 10% and watch error budget.

kevin: Re-weighed to 10%. Continuing to monitor.

jamal: Follow-up actions: create runbook for TF provider rate limits, add retry logic to our TF module CI wrapper, and queue infra postmortem.

maria: Filing runbook draft in #docs-infra, will link here when ready.

jamal: Thanks everyone — closing thread once postmortem ticket created.
